Adventure action continuation: native source reconstruction

Images are the two files configured by data/runtime/native-pe-images.json:
  Steam   PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  Classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
All addresses below are RVAs. The classic executable has the same modern
Adventure HUD producer and input branches as the Steam executable; classic
graphics selection does not substitute a different caption producer.

Native ownership
  viewscreen_dungeonmodest RTTI vtable:
    Steam 16b9f48; Classic 16b4e38.
  Virtual slot 1 (input):
    Steam 7f7020..8019fd; Classic 7f48a0..7ff27d.
  Virtual slot 2 (logic):
    Steam 7eed80..7f3ca2; Classic 7ec600..7f1522.
  Virtual slot 3 (render wrapper):
    Steam 7f3cb0..7f6c21; Classic 7f1530..7f44a1.
  Render wrapper mode word 2640b70 (classic 263aa60), values 0x19 or
  0x1a, selects legacy renderer 80d5e0 (classic 80ae60); the other modes
  select modern renderer af1190..b03c40 (classic aee1d0..b00c80).
  The render-mode-selection and legacy-render-dispatch assembly files
  preserve those real selection branches. The seven continuation captions
  and three waiting-dialog source lines have no other RIP-relative owner
  in either configured image; the legacy renderer has no equivalent
  finite-text branch. native-string-xrefs.tsv retains all of their image
  references, including repeated draws of Continue action and Stop action.

Continuation-control gate and state
  At af98a5 (classic af68e5), the renderer calls has_continuable_action
  7eeb70..7eed14 (classic 7ec3f0..7ec594), saving AL to local [rbp-6c].
  At afb3e8 (classic af8428), a false local gate skips the complete caption
  block and selects the icon-only HUD path beginning afba1d (classic
  af8a5d). True selects the captions below.
  player = *(23e5110), classic *(23df000).
  state = signed int8(player + 143c).

  if has_continuable_action:
      if state == 0:
          row_1 = key(0x52) + "Continue action"
          row_2 = key(0x53) + "Stop action"
          row_3 = key(0x54) + "Finish action"
      else if state == 1 and in_conflict(player):
          row_1 = key(0x52) + "Continue action"
          row_2 = key(0x53) + "Stop action"
          row_3 = key(0x54) + "In conflict! " + "Finish anyway"
      else if state == 2 or state == 1:
          row_1 = "Finishing up..."
          row_2 = key(0x53) + "Stop action"
          # No third caption is drawn in this branch.
      else:
          # No continuation caption is drawn for other state values.

  The state selector is afb40d..afb42b (classic af844d..af846b).
  The conflict predicate call is afb4a6 (classic af84e6).
  Normal producer begins afb81c (classic af885c).
  Conflict producer begins afb4b3 (classic af84f3).
  Finishing producer begins afb6fd (classic af873d).
  Shared post-caption path begins afb436 (classic af8476).

  Caption / literal RVA / native constructor operand instruction RVA:
    Continue action   Steam 16d1be0: afb52d, afb896
                      Classic 16ccba8: af856d, af88d6
    Stop action       Steam 16d1b70: afb5da, afb7e1, afb943
                      Classic 16ccb38: af861a, af8821, af8983
    In conflict!      Steam 16d1b90: afb679
                      Classic 16ccb58: af86b9
                      # Actual immutable literal ends with one ASCII space.
    Finish anyway     Steam 16d1ba0: afb6c2
                      Classic 16ccb68: af8702
    Finishing up...   Steam 16d1af0: afb746
                      Classic 16ccab8: af8786
    Finish action     Steam 16d1b80: afb9e2
                      Classic 16ccb48: af8a22

  These are six distinct source literals, including the normal, conflict
  and finishing variants. In conflict! and Finish anyway are consecutive,
  independent calls to draw_text on the same row. The first source keeps its
  trailing space, so the concatenated visible caption is exactly:
      "In conflict! Finish anyway"
  Each native string constructor uses 068150 (classic 0680e0), then
  draw_text ad9960 (classic ad69a0); no dynamic noun/name helper produces
  these six captions. These controls do not contain squad aliases.

Native continuation predicates (complete bodies retained)
  has_continuable_action 7eeb70 / classic 7ec3f0:
    If player state word +c6 is 0xd6 or 0xd7, or the unit referenced by
    player+3dc exists and its +c6 is 0xd0, compare +a8/+aa/+ac to
    +c0/+c2/+c4. Any differing coordinate returns true. Equal coordinates
    call 073a60 (classic 0739f0) and return false.
    Otherwise iterate native activity vector 24e3820..24e3828 (classic
    24dd710..24dd718), each activity's +8..+10 events. Require event
    virtual kind == 0xe, (event+14 & 0x1)==0, virtual slot +20 false,
    and an entry in event+e0..+e8 whose +8 matches player+130. Such an
    entry returns true; exhausted/empty vectors return false.
  in_conflict 643e00..643f67 / classic 641820..641987:
    Iterate the same activity vector. Require activity word +4 == 2,
    event virtual kind == 8, (event+14 & 0x1)==0. For each event+48..+50
    entry, query entry+8 using player+c30 and entry+20 using player+130.
    Either optional integer result other than -1 returns true. Empty
    collections, unmatched kinds, inactive events and all absent results
    reach the false return. This predicate produces no text.

Native input path
  Input saves the same has_continuable_action predicate at 7f761a (classic
  7f4e9a). True routes from 7f9b6e..7f9b94 (classic 7f73ee..7f7414)
  into action_input 7f6d60..7f7016 (classic 7f45e0..7f4896).
  That entire helper is retained, including pointer-tree key membership
  branches, click rectangles, subordinate-unit lookup and every return:
    key(0x52) or first click rectangle:
      set player+be0=1; invoke resume_action; return handled=true.
    key(0x53) or second click rectangle:
      invoke a40d90 then 073a60 on player (classic a3e5c0 / 0739f0).
      Look up player+3dc in unit vector 23e50b0..23e50b8 (classic
      23defa0..23defa8). If found, invoke those same two calls on it.
      Return handled=true; missing unit also returns handled=true.
    key(0x54) or third click rectangle:
      set player+be0=1; invoke resume_action.
      If old state==1 and in_conflict(player), set state=2;
      otherwise set state=1. Return handled=true.
    no matching key/click: return handled=false.
  resume_action 7f6c30..7f6d60 (classic 7f44b0..7f45e0) has chained
  unwind records; the retained span includes both returns and all branches.
  It calls 7e4e90 (classic 7e2710). If denied, return false. If allowed,
  conditionally clear event +2c fields, clear the native key set, snapshot
  player coordinates and time globals, and set action UI state 2649534=1
  (classic 2643424=1), with its adjacent counter/byte cleared.
  All above feed helpers and predicates have no caption-producing literal.

Independent waiting dialog, sharing the same native key-caption renderer
  action UI state 2649534 (classic 2643424) == 6 selects the waiting
  dialog at b035c5..b0386a (classic b00605..b008aa). Other values skip it.
  It creates a modal frame, then draws the following three independent
  prose rows, followed by one independent button:
    y=18: "You haven't been able to act for a while."
    y=19: "You can continue waiting, or save/quit from"
    y=20: "the settings menu."
    y=24: key(0x52) + "Continue waiting"
  The second and third rows form exactly the semantic sentence:
    "You can continue waiting, or save/quit from the settings menu."
  The three native rows are separate draw calls, not one native string.
  Their literal and operand addresses are in native-literals.tsv.
  The input state==6 branch is 7f763d..7f7794 (classic 7f4ebd..7f5014).
  key(0x52) or the waiting button rectangle clears the input and restores
  action UI state to 1; settings input uses its existing separate path.
  Continue waiting is related through its input-key renderer and action UI
  state, but it is independent from player+143c's three action variants.

Current-key text supplier (complete bodies retained)
  Each key() draw calls c394b0..c395b5 (classic c364f0..c365f5), which
  asks 8ecb30..8ece32 (classic 8ea360..8ea662) for the current binding.
  It selects the first actual entry's std::string at entry+20 from the
  key-binding tree 2390658 (classic 238a548). This string is configurable
  by the player; it is not a new finite action caption or a fixed R/S/T
  assumption. For absent/empty bindings the native visible source is "?",
  written inline at 8ecdf0 (classic 8ea620).
  "Missing binding displayed: " and its RIP-relative tail references are
  diagnostic stream text in that helper, not additional game UI captions.

Translation envelope
  The continuation family has the six immutable captions above, its
  actual same-row concatenation "In conflict! Finish anyway", and the
  independent waiting button plus three native prose rows. A translation
  can own the complete conflict caption while respecting both native
  component draws. No additional finite action caption is hidden in its
  direct helper paths. Binding strings and their "?" fallback retain the
  native key role. Files are native source extraction material only.
